messages.content: How can I sell my acoustic guitar?

function.name: tune_instrument
function.description: This function helps tune instruments based on the instrument type and the desired key or note. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

instrument_type.description: The type of the instrument, e.g. 'acoustic guitar', 'piano'.

key.description: The key or note to which the instrument should be tuned to. Default is 'Standard' for guitars.

message.content:
Here’s a step‑by‑step guide to help you sell your acoustic guitar quickly and safely: | Step | What to Do | Why It Matters | |------|------------|----------------| | **1. Clean & Tune** | Give the guitar a thorough cleaning (strings, fretboard, body). Tune it to standard pitch. | A well‑presented instrument looks more appealing and shows you’ve cared for it. | | **2. Take High‑Quality Photos** | Capture the whole body, headstock, strings, fretboard, and any imperfections. Use natural light and a neutral background. | Good photos attract buyers and reduce the chance of disputes over condition. | | **3. Research Market Value** | Check recent sales on Reverb, eBay, Craigslist, Facebook Marketplace, and local music stores. Note price ranges for similar models, ages, and conditions. | Helps you set a realistic price and avoid underselling. | | **4. Write a Detailed Description** | Include brand, model, year, serial number, wood type, finish, any upgrades, and a brief history. Mention any wear or repairs. | Transparency builds trust and reduces post‑sale questions. | | **5. Choose Your Selling Platform(s)** | • **Reverb** – great for musical instruments, global reach.
• **eBay** – auction or fixed price, large audience.
• **Craigslist / Facebook Marketplace** – local, no shipping hassles.
• **Local music shops** – consignment or direct sale. | Different platforms reach different buyer types; use one or two that fit your preference. | | **6. Set a Competitive Price** | Start slightly above your target to allow room for negotiation. Consider adding a “shipping included” option if selling online. | Buyers often expect to haggle; a higher starting point keeps you from selling too low. | | **7. Decide on Shipping vs. Local Pickup** | • **Local pickup**: safer, no shipping cost.
• **Shipping**: use a sturdy case, bubble wrap, and insured freight. | Shipping expands your market but adds cost and risk; weigh the pros/cons. | | **8. Prepare for Payment** | • **Cash**: safest for local sales.
• **PayPal / Venmo**: secure for online sales.
• **Escrow services**: for high‑value items. | Avoid scams by using reputable payment methods and verifying funds before handing over the guitar. | | **9. Meet Safely (if local)** | • Choose a public place (coffee shop, police station, or a friend’s house).
• Bring a friend or family member if possible.
• Verify the buyer’s ID and confirm payment before handing over the instrument. | Protects you from theft or fraud. | | **10. Finalize the Sale** | • Sign a simple bill of sale (include serial number, price, date, and both parties’ signatures).
• Keep a copy for your records. | Provides legal proof of transfer and protects both parties. | | **11. Follow Up** | • Ask the buyer for feedback if you’re using an online marketplace.
• Keep the buyer’s contact info for future resale or trade‑in opportunities. | Builds a reputation and may help future sales. | ### Quick Tips - **Avoid “too good to be true” offers**: If a buyer offers significantly more than market value, verify their identity and payment source. - **Use a guitar case**: Even if you’re selling locally, a case protects the instrument during transport. - **Consider a trade‑in**: Some music stores will offer a trade‑in value that can offset the cost of a new instrument. - **Keep receipts**: If you had recent repairs or upgrades, keep receipts to prove authenticity and condition. ### Sample Listing (Reverb) > **Title:** 2015 Yamaha FG800 Acoustic Guitar – Excellent Condition > **Description:** > • Brand: Yamaha > • Model: FG800 > • Year: 2015 > • Wood: Spruce top, mahogany back & sides > • Finish: Natural gloss > • Serial #: 12345678 > • Condition: Minor fret wear, no cracks, recently tuned and cleaned. > • Extras: Original case, extra strings, and a small repair kit. > • Price: $350 (negotiable) > • Shipping: Available (insured, $30). > **Photos:** [Attach 5–7 high‑resolution images] > **Contact:** Email or phone (safe method). Feel free to adapt this template to your own guitar’s specifics. Good luck with your sale!

We can provide steps: research market value, clean instrument, take photos, list on platforms (eBay, Craigslist, Facebook Marketplace, Reverb, local classifieds), set price, describe condition, shipping options, safety tips.
